faq.q: How much does Morse Injury Law charge?
faq.a: Morse Injury Law publishes a contingency fee, which means the fee is a share of what the case recovers and there is nothing to pay if it recovers nothing. The rate itself is not published, so ask for it in writing, along with how case expenses are handled and whether they come out of the recovery before or after the fee. The first consultation is free, which is the place to ask.

faq.q: Does Morse Injury Law offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. Morse Injury Law publishes a free initial consultation. The intake line is published as open around the clock.

faq.q: Where does Morse Injury Law have offices?
faq.a: Morse Injury Law publishes one office, in San Diego. Addresses and the Google listing behind each one are on this profile under Offices.

faq.q: Who are the attorneys at Morse Injury Law?
faq.a: Morse Injury Law names two attorneys on its own site, and each is listed on this profile with the page we read them from. They have not been checked against a state register: California does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

faq.a: Morse Injury Law scores 37 and sits at Verified. Passed: website and footprint. Could not be answered from any public source and therefore counts neither for nor against the firm: licensure, discipline and entity registration.
